description: Per-call latency/outcome telemetry for the bot's own bitFlyer API requests, appended by src/bot/exchange/resilience.py's ApiHealthRecorder. Purely observational (best-effort, swallow-all-errors) -- never on the trading path and never influences order decisions itself; consumed by src/bot/monitoring/aggregate.py to build the dashboard's API health tile.
source: src/bot/exchange/resilience.py: ApiHealthRecorder.record() appends one line per observed API call (both PAPER and LIVE), wired in via ApiObserver in src/bot/main.py.
retention: self-rotating: ApiHealthRecorder rotates the file to api_health.csv.1 (overwriting any previous .1) once it exceeds max_bytes (4,000,000 by default, checked every 200 writes), then starts a fresh file with just the header -- history beyond one rotation's worth is not kept.

ts.meaning: time the call was observed by the recorder
ts.notes: NOT an ISO-8601 string like most other datasets in this repo -- a bare int()/pandas.to_datetime without unit='s' will misparse this

endpoint_class.meaning: coarse grouping of the endpoint (e.g. order-placement vs read-only) used for condition-monitor bucketing
endpoint_class.notes: see src/bot/exchange/resilience.py for the exact class names in use

endpoint.meaning: the specific bitFlyer API path/method called

outcome.notes: see resilience.py's failure classification (SAFE_RETRY/AMBIGUOUS/REJECTED) for how this feeds retry decisions

condition.meaning: the exchange-condition-monitor's state at the time of this call

health.meaning: raw health string from bitFlyer's own /v1/gethealth, when available for this call
health.notes: blank when not applicable/unavailable, not a missing-data marker

known_defects: DATA QA 2026-09-05: this file had no schema entry at all as of the 2026-09-05 14:03 UTC owner-PC QUALITY.json run (1 of the 134 schema_undefined files) -- added post hoc from reading src/bot/exchange/resilience.py's ApiHealthRecorder (HEADER constant + record()); no live api_health.csv sample was available on the VM to cross-check column values against, only the writer code.

best-effort writer: every failure mode (unwritable path, full disk, a locked file on Windows) is silently swallowed by design (telemetry must never affect the trading path) -- an api_health.csv that stops growing, or is entirely absent, is not necessarily evidence the bot itself is unhealthy, only that this particular telemetry sink failed.

the file rotates in place (renamed to .1, then a fresh file with just the header) once it exceeds ~4MB -- a long-running deployment's api_health.csv only ever holds its most recent rotation's worth of calls plus whatever accumulated after the last rotation; it is not a full-history log.
